[/tikz]
The graph shows $y=3x-1$ and $y=-x+3$.
What is the solution of the two equations, as an ordered pair $(x,y)$?

options.why: Wrote the coordinates in the wrong order, swapping the $x$ and $y$ values of the crossing point.
Read the $y$-intercept of $y=-x+3$ instead of the point where the lines cross.

The graph shows $y=-x+4$ and $y=-x+1$.
How many simultaneous solutions do these two equations have?

options.text: None — the lines are parallel, so they never meet.
Exactly one, where the two lines cross.

Counted a solution per line instead of looking for a single shared point.
